name: Enzyme peel (papaya/pumpkin)
lead: An enzyme peel is a cosmetic exfoliating mask built around fruit-derived protein-digesting enzymes, most often papain from papaya, bromelain from pineapple, or enzymes from pumpkin. People use it to loosen and lift the dead cells sitting on the skin's surface, aiming for a smoother, brighter, more even-looking complexion without the stinging of an acid peel.

Papain is a cysteine protease obtained from papaya latex that breaks peptide bonds in proteins [1]. Bromelain is a similar mixture of protein-digesting enzymes from pineapple, and extracted bromelain is used in cosmetics manufacturing among other industries [2]. In an enzyme peel the idea is that these proteases act on the protein bonds holding surface cells together, so the dead layer comes away with a short-contact mask that is rinsed off.

Research on the products themselves is limited. A 2022 laboratory study of eleven commercial peels advertised as enzymatic measured their protease activity against casein, a generic protein substrate, and compared them with fresh pineapple and papaya [3]. No human trial of cosmetic enzyme peels has been published.
infobox: Topical papain drug products pulled by FDA, 2008 [1]

paras: Enzyme peels are applied as masks and rinsed off after a short contact time. Chemical peel references describe alpha hydroxy acid and beta hydroxy acid peels as the mildest acid peel categories, with stinging, redness and dryness as expected light effects [4]. Enzyme peels are marketed as an option that exfoliates through protein digestion instead of acidity, though enzyme peels are not themselves covered in that reference.

Pumpkin enzyme peels are usually sold alongside fruit acids and are popular in at-home facial care; papaya and pineapple masks draw on the long commercial use of papain and bromelain in cosmetics [1][2].

In the laboratory comparison, pineapple flesh showed the highest specific protease activity, and two of the eleven commercial enzyme peels showed sufficient activity against casein [3]. This work measured enzyme activity in jars and tubes, not effects on human skin, and it shows that enzyme content varies between products.

Outside cosmetics, topical papain ointments have been used to clear dead or contaminated tissue from ulcers and wounds, and bromelain-based debridement is approved in Europe for burns as NexoBrid [1][2]. This debridement of dead tissue is the same enzymatic principle that cosmetic peels borrow on a much milder scale.

In September 2008 the US FDA told companies to stop marketing unapproved topical papain drug products, citing reports of serious reactions including allergic reactions with low blood pressure and rapid heart rate [1]. People with latex allergy may also react to papain because latex and papaya are related sources [1]. Cosmetic enzyme peels are a separate product category from those drug products. Bromelain supplements have no confirmed dosage or long-term safety data, according to Wikipedia's summary [2].
No studies found. A 2022 laboratory study measured the enzyme activity of commercial peels but did not test skin outcomes [3].

card.summary: Fruit-enzyme exfoliating mask sold as a gentle peel; a lab study found most tested products had little enzyme activity, and no skin trials exist.
card.aka: Papaya enzyme peel, pumpkin enzyme peel, papain mask
card.note: Papain has caused allergic reactions; product enzyme activity varies.

quick.overview:
An enzyme peel uses fruit enzymes such as papain from papaya to loosen dead skin cells, and is marketed as milder than acid peels.

A 2022 lab study found that only two of eleven commercial products had sufficient protease activity, and no human trials were found.
quick.mechanism: Protease enzymes break protein bonds in surface skin cells, aiming for gentle exfoliation without acids.
quick.risks: Papain has been linked to allergic hypersensitivity reactions, and people with latex allergy may be at higher risk of reacting to papaya.

chain: Fruit proteases applied as a short-contact mask
Surface dead-cell protein bonds loosen and rinse away
angle.text: Users apply a papaya, pumpkin or pineapple enzyme mask for a few minutes and rinse it off, aiming for smoother texture and a fresher look without the redness acid peels can cause. Brands position it for sensitive or first-time peel users.
